strategy.summary: Reproduce the univariate smoother bug by building statsmodels at the buggy commit 51e6bab53568 (the pre-fix source tree) with the PR's test files, then running the unskipped measurement-disturbance comparison for TestMultivariateGeneralObsCov. On the buggy source the smoothed measurement disturbance is C_t^{-1} eps_t rather than eps_t, so the 1e-7 absolute comparison against the conventional smoother fails. On the fixed revision it passes with a discrepancy of about 1.2e-9. No numerical versions are documented by the evidence; numpy and scipy are chosen here and flagged as such.

system_packages: C compiler (gcc or clang) for the Cython extensions in statsmodels/tsa/statespace/_smoothers/_univariate.pyx.in
build_commands: python -m pip install cython meson-python ninja pytest
pinned_because: numpy 1.26.4 and scipy 1.13.1 are chosen by this plan, not documented: the evidence gives no numpy or scipy constraint and no era ceiling, so these versions are an inferred choice for a 2024-era statsmodels dev tree that still builds from source.
python 3.11 is chosen, not stated by the evidence.
The bug lives in compiled Cython code (_univariate.pyx.in), so the extension must be rebuilt at the buggy commit and again at the fixed commit; a stale build will not transition.

strategy.reproducing_test: statsmodels/tsa/statespace/tests/test_univariate.py::TestMultivariateGeneralObsCov::test_smoothed_measurement_disturbance (un-skipped by the PR, now assert_allclose with atol=1e-7), together with the parametrized check_smoother_output in test_multivariate_switch_univariate.py that now includes smoothed_measurement_disturbance
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision 51e6bab53568 the un-skipped TestMultivariateGeneralObsCov measurement-disturbance comparison fails with an AssertionError because the univariate output is C_t^{-1} eps_t and differs from the conventional smoother by up to about 124. On the fixed revision (head e9bab398a20181b6795acbf3db231e21db8c2267, with the same test files) the same test passes, with the discrepancy at about 1.2e-9 within the 1e-7 absolute tolerance. Only this fail-to-pass transition counts; no printed values are checked.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare conventional_results.smoothed_measurement_disturbance against univariate_results.smoothed_measurement_disturbance for the TestMultivariateGeneralObsCov model, and check that y_t - Z_t alpha_hat_t - eps_hat_t is near zero, using the identity the PR adds as a parametrized test.

input_output_examples.input: TestMultivariateGeneralObsCov model, smoothed measurement disturbance from univariate smoother
input_output_examples.expected_output: 1.2e-09 discrepancy after fix (agreement with conventional smoother within absolute tolerance 1e-7)

risks: Platform and toolchain: the bug is in compiled Cython code, so the buggy and fixed results depend on building the extension from the right commit. Stale .so files from another checkout will give false results.

The transition is specific to the non-diagonal observation covariance branch (model._diagonal_obs_cov == 0 and model._k_endog > 1). Single-endog or diagonal-covariance models do not exercise the triangular back-transform and will pass on both revisions.
The FILTER_CONVENTIONAL path is affected only through the fallback to univariate on singular F_t, so a plain conventional-filter run will not reproduce the bug.
Variates passed to the wrong method yield zero arrays and pass trivially. The test helper in the PR passes variates to simulate(), so check that the simulation-smoother tests are not comparing zeros.
The 5 pre-existing failures (test_plot_month, three test_forecast_index_types, TestGenericRLM::test_zero_collinear) are unrelated and should be excluded from the transition judgement.
ruff and flake8 are linters and do not test the numerical behaviour, so they are not part of the reproduction.
Numpy and scipy versions are unbounded in the evidence; a numpy 2.x build may change Cython or BLAS behaviour and the chosen 1.26.4 pin is an inference, not a documented requirement.

The numerical tolerance (1e-7 absolute) is taken from the PR; a platform with a looser or tighter floating-point baseline may shift the fixed-side discrepancy, though the buggy-side error of order 124 is far above any such shift.

oracle.reference_source: conventional smoother (filter_conventional=True) on the same model, as used in test_univariate.py
oracle.why: The conventional smoother returns eps_hat_t directly for a non-diagonal H_t, so agreement with it within 1e-7 absolute is the correctness check; the univariate result must match it after C_t premultiplication.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assert_allclose compares the conventional eps_hat_t against the univariate output, which on the buggy revision is C_t^{-1} eps_hat_t. The difference reaches about 124, far above the 1e-7 absolute tolerance, so the assertion raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the premultiplication by C_t in place, the univariate output equals the conventional eps_hat_t to within about 1.2e-9, below the 1e-7 absolute tolerance, so the assertion holds.
